Subject: NexaThera DPA — retention/backups carveout question

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our legal team reviewed the latest DPA redline and flagged a potential blocker around backups and DR. Specifically, we use ephemeral analytics logs (PII stripped) for 90 days, but our regulator requires that backups be retained for up to 180 days for certain audit purposes — which conflicts with the proposed "ephemeral retention" clause in section 4.2.

Attached is our annotated DPA redline (Nexa_DPA_redline_v3.docx) and a short FAQ on our backup/DR requirements (Backup-DR-FAQ.pdf).

Request: Can Redwood propose firm contract language that permits (1) ephemeral retention for primary logs (90 days), (2) an exception for regulator-mandated backups up to 180 days limited to encrypted cold storage, and (3) a clear deletion/derivative-data carveout for backups once retention ends?

We'd like to get this resolved before the SOW signature next week. Looping in our procurement lead Paul Chen on timelines.

Thanks,

— Samantha Ruiz

NexaThera Inc

Samantha — thanks for the clear ask and the docs. We're happy to work through a narrow carve-out that balances your regulatory needs and our platform guarantees.

I've looped in Kimberly (legal) and Rishi (security) to draft precise contract language. High-level approach we expect to propose:
- Keep 90-day ephemeral retention for primary analytics logs by default.
- Allow a controlled backup exception for regulator-flagged data with explicit scope: (a) limited to named categories, (b) stored encrypted at rest with customer-managed KMS option, (c) strict access controls and audit logging, and (d) automated purge at 180 days.
- Explicitly prohibit creating new derivatives from backup copies after purge, and require attestations of deletion.

I'll aim to get proposed redline language into DocuSign by Wednesday so your team can review ahead of SOW sign.

Ben / team / Samantha —

Thanks for the clear summary. I've reviewed Nexa's redline and drafted insertion language for the DPA to handle (i) ephemeral primary retention, (ii) limited backup exceptions, and (iii) deletion attestations. Key points in our proposed language (excerpted):

"4.2.a Ephemeral Primary Storage: Customer data designated as 'ephemeral analytics logs' shall be retained in primary serving systems for a period not to exceed ninety (90) days and shall be deleted in accordance with Redwood's documented deletion routines.

4.2.b Limited Backup Exception: Notwithstanding Section 4.2.a, Customer may request that Backup Copies containing Regulator-Mandated Records be retained in encrypted cold storage for a maximum period of one hundred eighty (180) days from the date of backup. Such Backup Copies shall: (i) be encrypted at rest using industry-standard AES-256 and, upon Customer request, can be encrypted using Customer-managed keys (KMS); (ii) be accessible only to personnel with documented approval and recorded in audit logs; (iii) be tagged and scoped to named data categories provided by Customer; and (iv) be subject to automated purge at the 180-day mark.

4.2.c No Derivative Use; Deletion Attestation: Backup Copies shall not be used to create derivative models, analytics or products. Upon purge of Backup Copies, Redwood shall provide Customer with an attestation of deletion including the time-stamp and the storage identifiers purged."

Open items for Nexa to confirm: (1) list of data categories that qualify as "Regulator-Mandated Records", (2) whether Nexa will require Customer-managed KMS or will accept Redwood-managed keys, and (3) whether Nexa wants audit log exports on a weekly basis or on request.

I've attached the excerpted redline into the DocuSign draft and left comments on the wordings around "derivative use" and "attestation".

-Kim
Kimberly Park

Kim / Ben —

Appreciate the careful language. NexaThera's responses inline below and attached updated category list.

> (1) list of data categories that qualify as "Regulator-Mandated Records"

Confirmed: The attached "Nexa_Mandated_Categories.xlsx" identifies Logs A (transaction traces), Logs C (authentication events), and a small subset of anonymized audit trails. Those are the only categories we expect to request backup retention for.

> (2) KMS: customer-managed keys?

Nexa prefers customer-managed keys for cold backups for liability reasons, but will accept Redwood-managed keys for non-regulatory data if that reduces operational friction.

> (3) audit log exports cadence

We request automated weekly audit log summaries by default and full exports on request during an audit window.

Counter-proposal on attestation: Instead of a weekly attestation on purge, we can accept a signed quarterly deletion report with metadata for any purge events that occurred that quarter.

We reviewed your DocuSign draft and left two comments in the envelope. Once those are resolved we'd like Redwood to send the final DPA envelope for signature (DocuSign link preferred).

Thanks — will try to get procurement to confirm SOW timeline once language is finalized.
